name: Rage Against the Machine
description:
'''Rage Against the Machine''' (often abbreviated as '''RATM''' or shortened to '''Rage''') was an American [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in Los Angeles, California, in 1991. It consisted of [[Zack de la Rocha]] (vocals), [[Tim Commerford]] (bass), [[Tom Morello]] (guitar), and [[Brad Wilk]] (drums). They melded [[Rap metal|heavy metal, rap]], [[punk rock]], and [[funk]] with [[anti-authoritarian]], [[Anti-capitalism|anti-capitalist]] and [[revolutionary]] lyrics. As of 2010, they had sold more than 16 million records worldwide. 

Rage Against the Machine released their [[Rage Against the Machine (album)|self-titled debut album]] in 1992 to acclaim; in 2020, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked it number 221 on its list of the [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time|500 greatest albums of all time]]. They achieved commercial success following their performances at the 1993 [[Lollapalooza]] festival. Their next albums, ''[[Evil Empire (album)|Evil Empire]]'' (1996) and ''[[The Battle of Los Angeles (album)|The Battle of Los Angeles]]'' (1999), topped the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] chart.

In 2000, Rage Against the Machine released the cover album ''[[Renegades (Rage Against the Machine album)|Renegades]]''. They disbanded in 2000 after de la Rocha quit, and the other members formed the band [[Audioslave]] with the singer [[Chris Cornell]]. After pursuing other projects, they reunited to perform at [[Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival|Coachella]] in 2007. Over the next four years, they played [[Rage Against the Machine reunion tour|live venues and festivals]] around the world before going on hiatus in 2011. In 2022, Rage Against the Machine began the [[Public Service Announcement Tour]]. It was cut short after de la Rocha suffered a leg injury. Wilk confirmed in 2024 that the band had disbanded for the third time.

Rage Against the Machine became a popular and influential band, and influenced the [[nu metal]] genre which came to prominence during the late 1990s and early 2000s. They were also ranked No. 33 on [[VH1]]'s ''100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock''. They were inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2023.
